about: Source list for the CLOSURES SUPER-BOT (kpc_closures_bot.py, RULE SHEET D). One row per page or feed: area (US-XX / CA-XX / 'US' for every state), agency, url, kind ('feed' = machine-readable, 'page' = read as text, 'pdf' = read by range), how (a reader name in the bot, or 'generic'), scope ('state' = state parks and WMAs only, 'federal' = federal units only, 'all'). The 49 pages of KPC-Links data/closure-pages.json are read too (loaded by the bot, not copied here) with how 'generic'. Chat 8 adds rows here; the bot lists a page once. Pages that block robots are reported 'robots' and never worked around. 'home' on a row = the unit's own park for notices that name no other POTA park (forests, refuges). 'districts' = the ranger districts of a multi-state forest inside each area.

sources.note: Kentucky's own reader (kpc_park_alerts.py) reads the same list; CL-5: that reader wins until Brandon's GO
SharePoint list: each alert is a link to its own page; the link text is the notice
KDFWR quota-hunt calendar (URL confirmed by chat 2 Oct 25 probe): table rows WMA | hunt | dates -> HUNT items (CL-2)
public-land hunting page: WMA closures to non-hunters with dates
home = the forest's own park: a forest-wide alert belongs to US-4484; a named WMA / trail on forest land gets it too (Sheet D ex. 5)
the fs.usda.gov/alerts/lbl page is 404 (Oct 28); this JetEngine page lists each alert as a dated paragraph
Georgia sheet GA1-GA4: 'Updated m/d/yy' = the agency date; vehicles-only = note; lease ended = 'may not be public land now'
GA4: quota hunts read like Kentucky's
also in closure-pages.json; listed here so a PDF list linked from it is read by range (CL-7)

districts.about: Ranger districts of multi-state national forests that lie IN this area (HQ Oct 28 fix 3): a notice from such a forest counts here only when it names this state, one of its counties, one of these districts, or a park here.

hunt_plugs_about: ONE HUNT PLUG PER STATE (Brandon Oct 28 9:00 PM: 'that won't work for every state'). A plug says where that state prints its per-area hunt dates and how to read them. kind 'quota-table-pdf' = a guide table (one row per area: number, area, dates) + the area's OWN page sentence that says it closes during the quota hunt (Fable Oct 29): table dates + closing sentence = a closure; a row whose area page has no closing sentence = a note (the area stays open). A state with NO plug gets NO invented closures: its cards show the state's hunting seasons + 'check <agency> for area closures' (fallback). New states come from chat 8's KPC_HuntClosureSources_desk.md; nothing new is shown without Brandon's GO.

US-KY.closing_rx: (?:\b(?:area|wma|property|portion|unit|tract|public|everyone|all (?:other )?(?:users|use|access))\b.{0,60}\bclos\w*.{0,120}\bquota hunts?\b|^\s*(?:the area is |is )?closed (?:during|for).{0,40}\bquota hunts?\b|\bclos\w* to all access\b.{0,120}\bquota\b|\bclosed during \(and day before\).{0,40}\bquota hunt)
US-KY.grey_area: G-H1 (for Brandon / chat 8): a WMA page that only says a deer SEASON is closed during the quota hunt ('Closed to archery/crossbow deer season during department-administered quota hunts') is filed as a NOTE (the area stays open), not 'closed to everyone'. The Oct 25 hand list files those WMAs as closed to everyone: rule which is right.
